newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 38.50 trln lire BOTs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 38.50 trln lire BOTs.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is expected to issue between 38 and 39.5 trillion lire of short term bills (BOTs) at its end-month auction against 42.25 trillion lire maturing, with the consensus estimate put at 38.50 trillion, a Reuter poll of analysts showed on Wednesday.

Analysts see the Treasury issuing 10.75 trillion lire of three-months bills (against 12 trillion maturing), 12.25 trillion lire of six-months bills (against 13.50 trillion maturing) and 15.50 trillion lire of one-year bills (16.75 trillion maturing).
The Treasury is also expected to issue 2.0 trillion lire of 18-months zero coupon certificate (CTZs) and 2.5 trillion lire of 24-months CTZs.

"The Treasury aims to renew the maturing paper, shifting part of the demand from BOTs to CTZs as to lengthen the average life of the debt and to postpone interest payment from 1997 to 1999," one analyst said.
"In this phase of the year, the Treasury needs funding and can not reduce the amount it will issue by much," another analyst said.
The Treasury will announce on Thursday January 23 the amounts of bills it will offer at this January 28 end of month auction. Settlement date for the bills is January 31.
